lines.line: Her movements used to be jerky, and this is how they were smoothed out.
Her poses change instantly. With nothing in between, her head and arms snapped from one pose to the next.
Now her upper body follows each pose through a critically damped filter. It takes about eighty milliseconds to catch up, and it never overshoots.
Her legs skip the filter, so her feet stay exactly where they are planted.
Her back still moved as if it were one stiff board, so each segment of her spine was given its own spring, which gets looser towards her head.
Now her back bends a little when she sets off, when she stops, and when she drops into the chair, and then it settles.
